*ā no bhadrā ityanena dīrghamāyurabāpnuyāt \|*  
*tvaṃ sīmeti ca sūktena navaṃ paśyenniśākaraṃ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*upatiṣṭhet samitpāṇirvvāsāṃsyāpnotyasaṃśayaṃ \|*  
*āyurīpsannimamiti kautsa sūktaṃ sadā jape \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. (One who repeats the hymn) ā no bhadrā\[20\] will get long life. One should look at the rising moon with (the repetition of) the hymn tvam soma and worship with the twig in the hand. He will certainly get garments. One who desires (long) life should always repeat the hymn of Kautsa (beginning with) imaṃ.

## \|\| 259.24 \|\|

*āpanaḥ śośucaditi stutvā madhye divākaraṃ \|*  
*yathā muñcati ceṣīkāṃ tathā pāpaṃ pramuñcati \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. By glorifying the Sun at midday with (the hymn) apanaḥ śośucad, one gets freed from sin like (a bow) when the arrow is discharged.

## \|\| 259.25-26 \|\|

*jātavedasa ityetajjapet svastyayanaṃ pathi \|*  
*bhayairvvimucyate sarvvaḥ svastimānāpnuyāt gṛhān \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vyuṣṭāyāñca tathā rātryāmetadduḥsvapnanāśanaṃ \|*  
*pramandineti sūyantyā japedgarbhavimocanaṃ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. One’s pathway becomes safe by the repetition of (the hymn) jātavedasa\[23\]. One gets free from all fears. That person enjoying auspicious things will get houses. This (hymn) destroys the bad dream of the previous night. One should repeat (the hymn) pramandina and (a woman) who is delivering a child will do so with ease.

## \|\| 259.27 \|\|

*japannindramiti snāto vai śvadevantu saptakaṃ \|*  
*muñcatyājyaṃ tathā juhvat sakalaṃ kilviṣaṃ naraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A man will get free from all sins after bathing with (the repetition of the hymn) upannindraṃ and offering clarified butter as oblation (while repeating) the seven Vaiśvadeva (hymns).

## \|\| 259.28-29 \|\|

*imāmiti japan śaśvat kāmānāpnotyabhīpsitān \|*  
*mānastoka iti dvābhyāṃ trirātropoṣitaḥ śuciḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*auḍumbarīśca juhuyātsamidhaścājyasaṃskṛtāḥ \|*  
*chittvā sarvvānmṛtyupāśān jīvedrogavivarjitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. One who repeats (the hymn) imām\[26\] always will get all his desires fulfilled. One who fasts for three nights and offers the twigs of udumbara (tree) dipped in clarified butter with (the repetition of) the two (hymns) mā nastoka etc. after becoming pure will cut all the fetters of death and live free from disease.

## \|\| 259.30-33 \|\|

*ūdrdhvavāhuranenaiva stutvā śambhuṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*mānastoketi ca ṛcā śikhābandhe kṛte naraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*adhṛṣyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ jāyate saṃśayaṃ vinā \|*  
*citramityupatiṣṭheta trisandhyaṃ bhāskaraṃ tathā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*samitpāṇirnaro nityamīpsitaṃ dhanamāpnuyāt \|*  
*atha svapneti ca japan prātarmadhyandine dine \|\| 32 \|\|*

*duḥsvapnañcārddate kṛtsnaṃ bhojanañcāpnuyācchubham \|*  
*ubhe pumāniti tathā rakṣoghnaḥ parikīrttitaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

30-3la. One who having glorified Lord Śambhu with (the repetition of) this hymn with arms raised, binds the tuft into a knot while repeating the hymn mānastoka, no doubt, becomes invincible by all beings.

31b-32a. One should worship the Sun daily at the three twilights with (the repetition of the hymn) citraṃ holding the twig. Thus he will get the desired wealth.

32b-33. One will destroy the entire bad dream and get good food by the repetition of (the hymn) atha svapna in the morning and noon everyday. (The hymn) ubhe pumān is said to destroy the demons.

## \|\| 259.34 \|\|

*ubhe vāsā iti ṛco japan kāmānavāpnuyāt \|*  
*na sāgānniti ca japan mucyate cātatāyinaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. One who repeats the hymn ubhe vāsā\[30\] will get all the pleasures. A person repeating (the hymn) na sāgan will escape from the murderer.

## \|\| 259.35 \|\|

*kayā śubheti ca japan jātiśraiṣṭhamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*imannṛsomamityetat sarvvān kāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. One who repeats (the hymn) kayā śubha\[32\] will attain caste-excellence, and (the hymn) imaṃ nṛsomaṃ will give all the pleasures.

## \|\| 259.36 \|\|

*pitarityupatiṣṭheta nityamarthamupasthitaṃ \|*  
*agne nayeti sūktena ghṛtahomaśca mārgagaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Conveying obeisance with (the hymn) pitaḥ\[34\] one will always acquire riches. Oblation made with ghee with (the repetition of the hymn) agne naya also shows the path.

## \|\| 259.37 \|\|

*vīrānnayamavāpnoti suślokaṃ yo japet sadā \|*  
*saṅkato neti sūktena viṣān sarvvān vyapohati \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. One who repeats suśloka\[36\] will always get a progeny of heroes. One is able to destroy all poisons by (the repetition of) the hymn kaṅkato na.

## \|\| 259.38 \|\|

*yo jāta iti sūktena sarvvān kāmānavāpnuyāt \|*  
*gaṇānāmiti sūktena snigdhamāpnotyanuttamaṃ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. One will get all the pleasures by (the repetition of) the hymn yo jāta\[38\]. One will get an excellent friend by (the repetition of) the hymn gaṇānām.

## \|\| 259.39-4 \|\|

*yo me rājannitīmāṃntu duḥsvapnaśamanīmṛcaṃ \|*  
*adhvani prasthito yastu paśyecchatruṃ samutthitaṃ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*aprasastaṃ praśastaṃ vā kuvidaṅga imaṃ japet \|*  
*dvāviṃśakaṃ japan sūktamādhyātmikamanuttamaṃ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*parvasu prayato nityamiṣṭān kāmān samaśnute \|*  
*kṛṇuṣveti japan sūktaṃ juhvadājyaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*gāyatryā daśasāhasro japo naktāśino dvija \|*  
*bahusnātasya tatraiva sarvakalpamanāśanaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

39-4la. (One should repeat) the hymn yo me rājan\[40\] that destroys bad dream. One who commences a journey and faces an unpraiseworthy or praiseworthy enemy should repeat the (hymn) kuvidaṅga\[41\]. One will enjoy all the desired pleasures by repeating the excellent hymn ādhyātmika consisting of twenty-two verses on the full and new moon days.

4Ib-43. One should offer an oblation of clarified butter with concentrated (mind) repeating the hymn kṛṇuṣva\[43\]. One will take away the lives of enemies and destroy even the demons (by this). One should worship daily the Fire (god) with the hymn pari\[44\]. The Fire (god) having a face on every side Himself protects that person on all sides. One should look at the Sun, (remaining) pure and (repeating) the (hymn) haṃsaḥ śuciṣad.

## \|\| 259.44-47 \|\|

*kṛṣiṃ prapadyamānastu sthālīpākaṃ yathāvidhi \|*  
*juhuyāt kṣetramadhye tu svanīsvāhāstu pañcabhiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*indrāya ca marudbyastu parjjanyāya bhagāya ca \|*  
*yathāliṅgantu viharellāṅgalantu kṛṣībalaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*yukto dhānyāya sītāyai sunāsīramathottaraṃ \|*  
*gandhamālyairnamaskārairyajedetāśca devatāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*pravāpane pralavane khalasītāpahārayoḥ \|*  
*amoghaṅgarmma bhavati varddhate sarvvadā kṛṣiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

44-47. A man about to cultivate a field should offer oblations of pot-boiled porridge at the centre of the field as laid down with the five (hymns) svanī svāhā. A farmer should derive his plough in the approriate manner (and offer oblations) to (the gods) Indra, Maruts, Parjanya and Bhaga. One should then worship Indra and these deities with perfumes, garlands and prostrations (after having worshipped) the ploughshare (saying) (the yoke) has been fastened for the sake of grains. Agriculture will thus always thrive and the work relating to sowing (the seeds), cutting, threshing and ploughing will yield profuse results.

## \|\| 259.48-49 \|\|

*samudrāditi sūktena kāmānāpnoti pāvakāt \|*  
*viśvānara iti dvābhyāṃ ya ṛgbhyāṃ vahnimarhati \|\| 48 \|\|*

*sa taratyāpadaḥ sarvvā yaśaḥ prāpnoti cākṣayaṃ \|*  
*vipulāṃ śriyamāpnoti jayaṃ prāpnotyanuttamaṃ \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. One will get the desired things from the Fire (god) by (the recitation of) the hymn samudrāt\[47\] One who worships the Fire (god) with the two hymns (called) viśvānara, surmounts all difficulties, gets undiminishing fame, abundant wealth and unsurpassed victory.

## \|\| 259.50 \|\|

*agne tvamiti ca stutvā dhanamāpnoti vāñchitaṃ \|*  
*prajākāmo japennityaṃ varuṇadaivatatrayaṃ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. One gets the desired riches by propitiating (the Fire god) with (the hymn) agne tvam. A person desirous of having progeny should repeat the three hymns of Varuṇa daily.

## \|\| 259.51-52 \|\|

*svastyā trayaṃ japet prātaḥ sadā svastyayanaṃ mahat \|*  
*svasti panthā iti procya svastimān vrajate'dhvani \|\| 51 \|\|*

*vijīgīṣurvanaspate śatraṇāṃ vyādhitaṃ bhavet \|*  
*striyā garbhapramūḍhāyā garbhamokṣaṇamuttamaṃ \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. (Each) morning, one should recite the three svasti\[50\] hymns, whereby one (will) always secure great prosperity. By the recitation of (the hymn) svasti panthām\[51\] one will have safe journey. One who desires to conquer (should repeat the hymn) vanaspate, (by which) enemies will be laid down with disease. (By the recitation of the same hymn) a woman having a dead foetus will have a good delivery.

## \|\| 259.53 \|\|

*acchāvadeti sūktañca vṛṣṭikāmaḥ prayojayet \|*  
*nirāhāraḥ klinnavāsā na cireṇa pravarṣati \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. One who is desirous to get rain should employ the hymn acchāvada after fasting and wearing wet clothes. It will rain in no time.

## \|\| 259.54 \|\|

*manasaḥ kāma ityetāṃ paśukāmo naro japet \|*  
*karddamena iti snāyātprajākāmaḥ śucivrataḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. A person who desires to have a cow should repeat (the hymn) manasaḥ kāma.\[54\] One who desires to have progeny should bathe (reciting the hymn) kardamena, after becoming pure and practising vow.

## \|\| 259.55-56 \|\|

*aśvapūrvā iti snāyādrājyakāmastu mānavaḥ \|*  
*rohite carmmaṇi snāyāt brāhmaṇastu yathāvidhi \|\| 55 \|\|*

*rājā carmmaṇi vaiyāghre chāge vaiśyastathaiva ca \|*  
*daśasāhasriko homaḥ pratyekaṃ parikīrttitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. A man who wants to acquire kingdom should bathe with (the repetition of the hymn) aśvapūrvāṃ. A brahmin should bathe (standing) on a deer-skin as laid down. A king (should bathe standing) on a tiger-skin and a man of the merchant class on a goat (skin) in the same way. It has been declared that ten thousand oblations (should be done) in each case.

## \|\| 259.57 \|\|

*āgāra iti sūktena goṣṭhe gāṃ lokamātaraṃ \|*  
*upatiṣṭhed vrajeccaiva yadicchettāḥ sadākṣayāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. If a person desires to have (the herds of cattle) always undiminshing (in his cowpen), he should worship the cow, the mother of the worlds, in the cowpen with (the recitation of) the hymn āgāvo.

## \|\| 259.58 \|\|

*upetitisṛbhī rājño dundubhimabhimantrayet \|*  
*tejo balañja prāpnoti śatruñcaiva niyacchati \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. A king should consecrate the (royal) drum with the three (hymns beginning with) upa. (By this) he will get radiance and strength and rout the enemy.

## \|\| 259.59 \|\|

*tṛṇapāṇirjjapetsūktaṃ rakṣoghnaṃ dasyubhirvṛtaḥ \|*  
*ye ke ca jmetyṛcaṃ japtvā dīrghamāyuravāpnuyāt6 \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. One who is surrounded by the demons should repeat the hymn rakṣoghnam\[59\] holding grass in the hand. By repeating the hymn ye ke ca jama one will gain long life.

## \|\| 259.60 \|\|

*jamūtamṛktena tathā senāṅgānyabhimantrayet \|*  
*yadhā liṅgaṃ tato rājā vinihanti raṇe ripūn \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. One should consecrate the constituents of his army by the hymn jīmūta first like a liṅga. Then the king will destroy the enemies in the battle.

## \|\| 259.61-62 \|\|

*āgneyeti tribhiḥ sūktairdhanamāpnoti cākṣayaṃ \|*  
*amīvaheti sūktena bhūtāni sthāpayenniśi \|\| 61 \|\|*

*saṃbādhe viṣame durge bandho vā nirgataḥ kkacit \|*  
*palāyan vā gṛhīto vā sūktametattathā japet \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. One will gain undiminishing wealth by (the recitation of) the three hymns (beginning with) āgneya\[62\]. One may fix goblins by (the repetition of) the hymn amīvaha in the night. One should repeat this hymn in danger, difficulty, when caught in a fort, taken as a prisoner, while setting out some time, while running away, or when held as a captive.

## \|\| 259.63-65 \|\|

*trirātraṃ niyatopoṣya śrāpayet pāyasañcaruṃ \|*  
*tenāhutiśataṃ pūrṇaṃ juhuyāt tryambaketyṛcā \|\| 63 \|\|*

*samuddiśya mahādevaṃ jīvedabdaśataṃ sukhaṃ \|*  
*taccakṣurityacā snāta upatiṣṭheddivākaraṃ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*udyantaṃ madhyāgañcaiva dīrghamāyurjjijīviṣuḥ \|*  
*indrā someti sūktantu kathitaṃ śatrunāśanaṃ \|\| 65 \|\|*

63-64a One should fast for three nights with self-control, boil sweat gruel and cast one hundred oblations with that with (the repetition of) the hymn tryambaka in honour of (Lord) Śiva. One will thus live happily for hundred years.

64b-65. One should worship the rising Sun and the Sun at the middle (of the day) after bathing and with the hymn taccakṣuḥ\[65\] if one desires to have long life. The hymn (called) indrā soma, (when repeated), is said to destroy the enemy.

## \|\| 259.66 \|\|

*yasya luptaṃ vrataṃ mohādvrātyairvā saṃsṛjetsaha \|*  
*upoṣyājyaṃ sa juhuyāttvamagne vratapā iti \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. A person who has lost his vow by mistake or on account of association with the vrātyas\[67\], should fast and offer oblation with clarified butter with (the recitation of the hymn) tvamagne vratapā.

## \|\| 259.67 \|\|

*ādityetyṛk ca samrājaṃ japtvā vāde jayī bhavet \|*  
*mahīti ca catuṣkeṇa mucyate mahato bhayāt \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. A person who repeats the hymn āditya\[69\] and samrāja\[70\] will get victory in debate. One will become free from great fear by (the repetition of) the four (hymns beginning with) mahī.

## \|\| 259.68 \|\|

*ṛcaṃ japtvā yadi hyetat sarvvakāmānavāpnuyāt \|*  
*dvācatvāriṃśatiṃ caindraṃ japtvā nāśayate ripūn \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. One will get all the pleasures by the repetition of the hymn yadi hyetat\[72\]. One will destroy his enemies by the repetition of the forty-two aindra hymns.

## \|\| 259.69-70 \|\|

*vācaṃ mahīti japtvā ca prāpnotyārogyameva ca \|*  
*śanno bhaveti dvābhyāntu bhuktvānnaṃ prathataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*hṛdayaṃ pāṇinā spṛṣṭvā vyādhibinnābhibhūyate \|*  
*uttabhedamiti snāto hutvā śatruṃ pramāpayet \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. One gets good health by repeating (the hymn) vācāmahī\[74\]. A person who eats food repeating the two (hymns) śanno bhava\[75\] after becoming clean and controlling the senses and touches the heart with the hand will not be attacked by diseases. One will destroy the enemy by offering oblations with (the hymns) uttamedaṃ after bathing.

## \|\| 259.71 \|\|

*śannogna iti sūktena hutenānnamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*kanyā vārarṣisūktena digdoṣādvipramucyate \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. One will get food by making oblation with the hymn śanno'gnir\[77\]. One will get free from the defects of the quarters (on journey) by (repeating) the hymn kanyāvārarṣi.

## \|\| 259.72 \|\|

*yadatya kavyetyudite japte'vaśyaṃ jagadbhavet \|*  
*yadvāgiti ca japtena vāṇī bhavati saṃskṛtā8 \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. One is able to subjugate the whole universe by the repetition (of the hymn) yadetya kavyaś\[79\] at (sun) rise. One’s speech gets refined by the repetition of (the hymn) yadvāk.

## \|\| 259.73 \|\|

*vāco vidamiti tvetāṃ japan vācaṃ samaśnute \|*  
*pavitrāṇāṃ pavitrantu pāvamānyeyṛco matāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. One gill get good speech by repeating (the hymn) vāco vidaṃ\[81\]. The pāvamāny hymns are considered to be most sacred.

## \|\| 259.74 \|\|

*vaikhānasāṛcastriṃśatpavitrāḥ paramā matāḥ \|*  
*ṛco dviṣaṣṭiḥ proktāśca parasvetyṛṣisattama \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The thirty vaikhānasa\[83\] hymns are considered to be extremely sacred. O Foremost among the sages! the parasva hymns are said to be sixty-two.

## \|\| 259.75 \|\|

*sarvvakalmaṣanāśāya pāvanāya śivāya ca \|*  
*svādiṣṭayetisūktānāṃ saptaṣaṣṭirudāhṛtā \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The sixty-seven hymns—svādiṣṭayā—are declared as destroyers of all sins, purifiers and conferrers of welfare.

## \|\| 259.76 \|\|

*daśottarāṇyṛcāñcaitāḥ pāvamānyaḥ śatāni ṣaṭ \|*  
*etajjapaṃśca juhvacca ghoraṃ mṛtyubhayaṃ jayet \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The six hundred and ten hymns of pāvamānya when repeated and used for making oblations will enable one to conquer the dread of death.

## \|\| 259.77 \|\|

*āpohiṣṭheti vāristho japetpāpabhayārddane \|*  
*pradevanneti niyate japecca marudhanvasu \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. One should repeat (the hymns) āpo hiṣṭha while standing in the water to destroy the fear of sin. A man passing through a desert should repeat (the hymn) pradevanna after the control (of senses).

## \|\| 259.78 \|\|

*prāṇāntike bhaye prāpte kṣipramāyustu vindati \|*  
*prāveyābityṛcamekāṃ japecca manasā niśi \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. When one is haunted by the fear of death, one will get (the end of) his life quickly. One should repeat the single hymn prāveyābhi mentally in the night.

## \|\| 259.79 \|\|

*vyuṣṭāyāmudite sṛryye dyute jayamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*mā pragāmeti mūḍhaśca panthānaṃ pathi vindati \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. (If it is repeated) at dawn or at sunrise one will get victory in gambling. One who has lost his way will find his way by (repeating the hymn) mā pragāma.

## \|\| 259.80-82 \|\|

*kṣīṇāyuriti manyet yaṅkañcit suhṛdaṃ priyaṃ \|*  
*yakteyamiti tu ratnātastasya mūrddhānamālabhet \|\| 80 \|\|*

*sahasrakṛtvaḥ pañcāhaṃ tenāyurvindate mahat \|*  
*idaṃ medhyeti juhuyāt ghṛtaṃ prājñaḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*paśukāmo gavāṃ goṣṭhe arthakāmaścatuṣpathe \|*  
*vayaḥ suparṇa ityetāṃ japan vai vindate śriyaṃ \|\| 82 \|\|*

80-8la. If one thinks that the life of a friend of himself is running out, he should bathe and touch the head of the friend (reciting the hymn) yatteyam thousand times for five days. He will thus find him long-lived.

81b-82. A wise man should offer a thousand oblations with ghee with (the repetition of the hymn) idam medhya\[91\]. One who desires to have cattle (should do it) at the cowpen and one who desires riches, at the crossroads. One who repeats (the hymn vayaḥ suparṇā will acquire wealth.

## \|\| 259.83 \|\|

*iviṣyantīyamabyasya sarvvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*tasya rogā vinaśyanti kāyāgnirvarddhate tathā \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. One will become free from all sins by the repetition of (the hymn) haviṣyantīyam. His diseases will get cured and the digestive power increased.

## \|\| 259.84 \|\|

*yā oṣadhayaḥ svastyayanaṃ sarvvavyādhivināśanaṃ \|*  
*vṛhaspate atītyetadvṛṣṭikāmaḥ prayojayet \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. (The hymn) yā oṣadhayaḥ\[94\] (when repeated) is a means of securing prosperity and curing all the diseases. One who wishes to have rain should employ (the hymn) bṛhaspate ati.

## \|\| 259.85 \|\|

*sarvvatreti parā śāntirjñeyā pratirathastathā \|*  
*sūta saṃkāśyapannityaṃ prajākāmasya kīrttitaṃ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. (The hymns) sarvatra\[96\] and pratiratha\[97\] are known (to confer) supreme peace. (The recitation of the hymn) sūta saṅkāśyapaṃ daily is commended for a person desirous to have progeny.

## \|\| 259.86 \|\|

*ahaṃ sdreti ityetadvāgmī bhavati mānavaḥ \|*  
*na yonau jāyate vidvān japanratīti rātriṣu \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. A person who (recites the hymn) ahaṃ rudra\[99\] becomes an eloquent speaker. The learned person who recites (the hymn) rāti in the nights is not born again.

## \|\| 259.87 \|\|

*rātrisuktaṃ japanrātrau rātriṃ kṣemī nayennaraḥ \|*  
*kalpayantīti ca cajapannityaṃ kṛttvārināśanaṃ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. The person who recites the rātrisūkta\[101\] in the night spends the night safely. By doing the recitation of (the hymn) kalpayantī daily (one will be able to) destroy the enemies.

## \|\| 259.88 \|\|

*āyuṣyañcaiva varccasyaṃ sūktaṃ dākṣāyaṇaṃ mahat \|*  
*uta devā iti japedāmayaghnaṃ dhṛtavrataḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. (The recitation of) the great Dākṣāyaṇa\[103\] hymn confers longevity and radiance. A person who has undertaken a vow should recite (the hymn) uta devā, that will destroy the diseases.

## \|\| 259.89 \|\|

*ayaptagne janityetajjapedagnibhaye sati \|*  
*araṇyānītyaraṇyeṣu japettadbayanāśanaṃ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. When there is fear from fire, one should recite the hymn ayamagne janī\[105\]. One should repeat (the hymn) araṇyānī in the forests to destroy the fear therein.

## \|\| 259.90 \|\|

*vrāhmīmāsādya sūkte dve ṛcaṃ cabrāhmīṃ śatāvarīṃ \|*  
*pṛthagadbhirghṛtairvātha medhāṃ lakṣmīñca vindati \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. (One who recites the two hymns) with devotion to (goddess) Brāhmi (the goddess of speech) (and makes use of) brāhmī and śatāvarī (the two herbs) together with water or ghee separately will gain intelligence and wealth.

## \|\| 259.91 \|\|

*māma ityasapatnaghnaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ vijigīṣataḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇogniḥ saṃvidānaṃ garbhamṛtyunivāraṇaṃ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. One who desires to conquer his enemy in the battle (should recite the hymn) māsa\[108\]. (The repetition of the hymn) brahmaṇo'gniḥ saṃvidānaṃ prevents the death of the child in the womb.

## \|\| 259.92 \|\|

*apaihīti japetsūktaṃ śuṣirdusvapnanāśanaṃ \|*  
*yenedamiti vai japtvā samādhiṃ vindate paraṃ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. After getting pure one should recite the hymn apaihi\[110\], that destroys (the effects of) bad dreams. One gains supreme concentration by the repetition of (the hymn) yenedaṃ.

## \|\| 259.93 \|\|

*mayo bhūrvvāta ityetat gavāṃ svastyayanaṃ paraṃ \|*  
*śāmvarīmindrajālaṃ vā māyāmetena vārayet \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. (The recitation of the hymn) mayo bhūrvāto is an excellent means of securing the welfare of the cattle. One will ward off sorcery or jugglery by (the repetition of) this (hymn).

## \|\| 259.94 \|\|

*mahītrīṇāmavarastviti pathi svastyayanaṃ japet \|*  
*agnaye bidviṣannevaṃ japecca ripunāśanaṃ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. One should repeat (the hymn) mahī trīṇāmavaro'stu\[113\] for securing one’s welfare on his journey. One should repeat (the hymn) agnaye vidviṣan, which will destroy the enemies.

## \|\| 259.95-96 \|\|

*vāstoṣpatena mantreṇa yajet gṛhadevatāḥ \|*  
*japasyaiṣa vidhiḥ prokto hute jñeyo viśeṣataḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*homānte dakṣiṇā deyai pāpaśāntirhutena tu \|*  
*hutaṃ śāmyati cānnena annahemapradānataḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

95-96. The presiding deities of the houses should be worshipped with the hymn vāstoṣpate. The procedure relating to the repetition has been told. That relating to the oblation has to be known as different. The (prescribed) fee has to be paid at the end of the oblation. (There will be) expiation of the sin by (offering) an oblation. The oblation done with food appeases by the offer of food and gold as gift.

## \|\| 259.97-99 \|\|

*viprāśiṣastvamoghāḥ syuṣaṃhiḥsnānantu sarvataḥ \|*  
*siddhārthakā yavā dhānyaṃ payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ tathā \|\| 97 \|\|*

*kṣīravṛkṣāstathedhmantu hāmā vai sarvakāmadāḥ \|*  
*samipaḥ kaṇṭakinyaśca rājikā rudhiraṃ viṣaṃ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*abicāre tathā śailaṃ aśanaṃ śaktavaḥ pathaḥ \|*  
*dadhi bhaikṣyaṃ phalaṃ mṛlamṛgvidhānamudāhṛtaṃ \|\| 99 \|\|*

97-99. The blessings of brahmins will be unfailing. One should bathe outside in every case. Oblations made with the white mustard, barley, grains, milk, curd, ghee and the twigs of the kṣīravṛkṣa-s\[116\], yield all the pleasures. The twigs of thorny (trees), black mustard, blood, poison and stone (are used as oblation) in incantation. Śaktu, milk, curd, food collected as alms, fruits and roots are the food while offering an oblation. Thus the use of the hymns of Ṛgveda has been explained.

## Chapter 260 - The use of the hymns of Yajurveda (yajurvidhāna)

## \|\| 260.1-2 \|\|

*athonaṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ \|*  
*yajurvidhānaṃ \|*  
*puṣkara uvāca \|*  
*yajurvidhānaṃ vakṣyāmi bhuktimuktipradaṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*oṃkārapūrvvikā rāma mahāvyāhṛtayo matāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sarvvakalmaṣanāśinyaḥ sarvvakāmapradāstathā \|*  
*ājyāhutisahasreṇa devānārādhayedbudhaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Puṣkara said:

1-2. I shall describe the use (of the hymns) of Yajur (veda) \[i.e., yajurvidhāna\], that yield enjoyment and emancipation. Listen (to me): O Rāma: The great vyāhṛtis are considered to be preceded by the syllable oṃ. They destroy all sins and yield all pleasures. A wise man should worship the gods with thousand oblations of clarified butter.

## \|\| 260.3 \|\|

*manasaḥ kāṅkṣitaṃ rāma manasepsitakāmadaṃ \|*  
*śāntikāmo yavaiḥ kuryyāttilaiḥ pāpāpanuttaye \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O Rāma: This confers the desired pleasures. One who desires peace should offer (oblation) with barley. (One should offer) with sesamum for the destruction of sin.

## \|\| 260.4 \|\|

*dhānyaiḥ siddhārthakaiścaiva sarvvakāma karaistathā \|*  
*audumbarībhiridhmābhiḥ paśukāmasya śasyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. (One should offer oblation) with grains and white mustard that will confer all the pleasures. (Offering oblations) with the twigs of udumbara (tree) is commended for one who desires cattle.

## \|\| 260.5 \|\|

*dadhnā caivānnakāmasya payasā śāntimicchataḥ \|*  
*apāmārgasamiddhastu kāmayan kanakaṃ bahu \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. One who desires food (should offer oblation) with curd and one who desires peace (should) with milk. One who desires plenty of gold (should offer oblation) with the twigs of apāmārga.

## \|\| 260.6 \|\|

*kanyākāmo ghṛtāktāni yugmaśo grathitāni tu \|*  
*jātīpuṣpāṇi juhuyādgrāmārthī tilataṇḍulān \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. One who seeks a maiden should offer oblation of jāti flowers that have been strung together in pairs and soaked in ghee. One who desires to have (governorship over) a village should offer (oblations of) sesamum and rice.

## \|\| 260.7 \|\|

*vaśyakarmmaṇi śākhoḍhavāsāpāmārgameva ca \|*  
*viṣāsṛṅmiśrasamidho vyādhighātasya bhārgava \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The oblations (of the twigs) of śākhoṭa, vāsā and apāmārga (trees) (are commended) for bringing (others) under control. O Son of Bhṛgu (Paraśurāma): (oblation) of twigs mixed with poison and blood (should be made) for causing the death of one after becoming sick.

## \|\| 260.8-9 \|\|

*kruddhastu juhuyātsamyak śatrūṇāṃ badhakāmyayā \|*  
*sarvvavrīhimayīṃ kṛtvā rājñaḥ pratikṛtiṃ dvija \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sahasraśastu juhuyādrājā vaśagato bhavet \|*  
*vastrakāmasya puṣpāṇi darvvā vyādhivināśinī \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. One who is angry (should act) perfectly in the above manner in order to kill his enemies. O Brahmin: After having made an image of the king made up of rice one should offer a thousand oblations. The king will thus be subjected to one’s control. Flowers (are to be used) by one who desires clothes. (The offering of) dūrvā (grass) destroys disease.

## \|\| 260.10 \|\|

*brahmavarccasakāmasya vāsograñca vidhīyate \|*  
*pratyaṅgireṣu juhuyāttuṣakaṇṭakabhasmabhiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. It is laid down that strong scents (should be used) by one who desires to gain the splendour of a realised soul. Oblation should be offered with the ash of husk and thorns in retaliatory enchantments.

## \|\| 260.11-12 \|\|

*vidveṣaṇe ca pakṣmāṇi kākakauśikayostathā \|*  
*kāpilañca ghṛtaṃ hutvā tathā candragrahe dvija \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vacācūrṇena sampātātsamānīya ca tāṃ vacāṃ \|*  
*sahasramantritāṃ bhuktvā medhāvī jāyate naraḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. (In incantation) to cause animosity, the wings of a crow and owl (should be offered). O Brahmin! One should offer the ghee of a black cow to fire at (the time of) the lunar eclipse and partake of it after having mixed it with the residue of powdered vacā (a kind of aromatic root) after incantation a thousand times. This will make him intelligent.

## \|\| 260.13-15 \|\|

*ekādaśāṅgulaṃ śaṅku lauhaṃ khādirameva ca \|*  
*dviṣato badhosīti japannikhanedripuveśmani \|\| 13 \|\|*

*uccāṭanamidaṃ karmma śatrūṇāṃ kathitaṃ tava \|*  
*cakṣuṣyā iti japtvā ca vinaṣṭañcakṣurāpnuyāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

*upayuñjata ityedanuvākantathānnadaṃ \|*  
*tanūnapāgne saditi dūrvvāṃ hutvārttivarjjitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-14a. A peg of eleven inches made of iron or khadira (tree) should be buried in the house of the enemy after repeating (the hymn dviṣato vadho'si. This act of magical incantation for (the destruction of) the enemy has been narrated to you.

14b-15. By the recitation of (the hymn) cakṣuṣyā\[3\] one will get back lost eyesight. (The repetition) of the section (of the hymn beginning with) upayuñjata\[4\] will procure food. One will be free from difficulties by offering oblation of dūrvā (grass) (with the recitation of the hymn) tanūnapāgne sat.

## \|\| 260.16-18 \|\|

*bheṣajamasīti dadhyājyairhomaḥ paśūpasarganut \|*  
*triyamvakaṃ yajāmahe homaḥ saubhāgyavarddhanaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kanyānāma gṛhītvā tu kanyālābhakaraḥ paraḥ \|*  
*bhayeṣu tu japannityaṃ bhayebhyo vipramucyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dhustūrapuṣpaṃ saghṛtaṃ hutvā syāt sarvakāmabhāk \|*  
*hutvā tu guggulaṃ rāma svapne paśyati śaṅkaraṃ \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. Oblation made with curd and clarified butter (with the recitation of the hymn) bheṣajamasi\[6\] will cure the sickness of domestic animals. Oblation (made with the recitation of the hymn) tryambakaṃ yajāmahe will increase one’s fortune. (One who makes an oblation with this hymn) pronouncing the name of a maiden, will secure that maiden. One who repeats (this hymn) daily when he is stricken with fear, will get free from fears. By making an oblation with the dhuttūra flower along with ghee (repeating this hymn), one will get all the pleasures. O Rāma! One who makes an oblation with guggulu (a fragrant gum resin) (with the recitation of the hymn) will see Śaṅkara (Śiva) in the dream.

## \|\| 260.19-20 \|\|

*yuñjate mano 'nuvākaṃ japtvā dīrghāyurāpnuyāt \|*  
*viṣṇoravāṭamityetat sarvabādhāvināśanaṃ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*rakṣoghnañca yaśasyañca tathaiva vijayapradaṃ \|*  
*ayatno agnirityetat saṃgrāme vijayapradaṃ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. One will get long life by repeating the section yuñjate mana\[8\]. (The repetition of the hymn) viṣṇorarāṭaṃ\[9\] destroys all the obstacles. It is capable of destroying demons. It also confers victory. (The repetition of the hymn) ayaṃ no agniḥ yields victory in battle.

## \|\| 260.21-22 \|\|

*idamāpaḥ pravahata snāne pāpāpanodanaṃ \|*  
*viśvakarmmannu haviṣā sūcīṃ lauhīndaśāṅgulām \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kanyāyā nikhaneddvāri sā 'nyasmai na pradīyate \|*  
*deva savitaretena hutenaitena cānnavān \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. (The hymn) idamāpaḥ pravahata\[11\] (when repeated) while bathing is capable of destroying sins. If one buries an iron nail of ten inches length at the threshold (of the house) of a maiden with (the repetition of the hymn) viśvakarmannu havis\[12\] she will not be given (in marriage) to somebody else. One who makes an oblation with (the repetition of the hymn) deva-savitaḥ will get food.

## \|\| 260.23-24 \|\|

*agnau svāheti juhuyādbalakāmo dvijottama \|*  
*tilairyavaiśca dharmmajña tathāpāmārgataṇḍulaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sahasramantritāṃ kṛtvā tathā gorocanāṃ dvija \|*  
*tilakañca tathā kṛtvā janasya priyatāmiyāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. O Knower of virtue! The excellent brahmin who desires strength should do oblation with sesamum, barley, rice and (twigs of) apāmārga with (the recitation of) agnau svāhā (oblations to fire). O Brahmin! One will win the affection of the people by making a mark (on the forehead) with gorocanā (yellow pigment got from the belly of cow) after having made the incantation (of the sacred syllable) a thousand times.

## \|\| 260.25-28 \|\|

*rudrāṇāñca tathā japyaṃ sarvvāghavinisūdanaṃ \|*  
*sarvvakarmmakaro homastathā sarvvatra śāntidaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ajāvikānāmaśvānāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ tathā gavāṃ \|*  
*manuṣyāṇānnarendrāṇāṃ bālānāṃ yoṣitāmapi \|\| 26 \|\|*

*grāmāṇāṃ nagarānāñca deśānāmapi bhārgava \|*  
*upadrutānāṃ dharmmajña vyādhitānāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

*marake samanuprāpte ripuje ca tathā bhaye \|*  
*rudrahomaḥ parā śāntiḥ pāyasena ghṛtena ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

25-28. The repetition of the Rudra (hymns) is capable of destroying all the sins. The oblation (made with that hymn) accomplishes all tasks and ensures peace everywhere. O Bhārgava! Knower of virtue! when the goats, sheep, horses, elephants, cows, men, kings, children, women, villages, cities and countries are being attacked or afflicted by diseases, when there is the outbreak of plague and there is fear from the enemies, then (the offering) of oblation with Rudra hymns with sweet porridge and ghee (will confer) supreme peace.

## \|\| 260.29-30 \|\|

*kuṣmāṇḍaghṛtahomena sarvvān pāpān vyapohati \|*  
*śaktuyāvakabhaikṣāśī naktaṃ manujasattama \|\| 29 \|\|*

*bahiḥsnānarato māsānmucyate brahmahatyayā \|*  
*madhuvāteti mantreṇa homādito 'khilaṃ labhet \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. One gets free from all sins by offering oblation with pumpkin and ghee (with the Rudra hymns). Excellent man! One gets free from (the sin of) killing a brahmin by eating the flour of barley, barley or alms in the night and bathing for a month outside. One will get everything by offering oblation with (the repetition of) the hymn madhuvātā.

## \|\| 260.31 \|\|

*dadhi krāvneti hutvā tu putrān prāpnotyasaṃśayaṃ \|*  
*tathā ghṛtavatītyetadāyuṣyaṃ syāt ghṛtena tu \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. One will certainly get children by offering oblation (with the recitation of the hymn) dadhikrāvṇa.\[16\] Similarly (oblation made) with ghee (with the recitation of the hymn) ghṛtavatī will give life.

## \|\| 260.32 \|\|

*svastina indra ityetatsarvvabādhāvināśanaṃ \|*  
*iha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvamiti puṣṭivivardhanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. (The recitation of the hymn) svasti na indra\[18\] would destroy all difficulties (and the hymn) iha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvaṃ would increase the strength.

## \|\| 260.33-34 \|\|

*ghṛtāhutisahasreṇa tathālakṣmīvināśanaṃ \|*  
*śruveṇa devasya tveti hutvāpāmārgataṇḍulaṃ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*mucyate vikṛtācchīghramabhicārānna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*rudra pātu palāśasya samidbhiḥ kanakaṃ labhet \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. A thousand oblations made with ghee (with this hymn) will ward off ill-luck. (Oblations made) with (the twigs of) apāmārga and rice (with the recitation of the hymn) sruveṇa devasya tvā\[20\] will without any doubt free one quickly from the deformities inflicted by incantation. One would get gold by (oblations) with the twigs of palāśa with (the hymn) rudra pātu (Rudra protect).

## \|\| 260.35 \|\|

*śivo bhavetyagnyutpāte vrīhibhirjuhuyānnaraḥ \|*  
*yāḥ senā iti caitacca taskarebhyo bhayāpaham \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. One should offer oblations with rice with (the recitation of the hymn) śivo bhava\[22\] (The repetition of the hymn) yāḥ senā removes the fear of thieves.

## \|\| 260.36 \|\|

*yo asmabhyamavātīyāddhutvā kṛṣṇatilānnaraḥ \|*  
*sahasraśo 'bhicārācca mucyate vikṛtāddvija \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O Brahmin! One who makes a thousand oblations with black sesamum with (the recitation of the hymn) yo asmabhyamayātīyāt will become free from deformities caused by incantation.

## \|\| 260.37 \|\|

*annenānnapatetyevaṃ hutvā cānnamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*haṃsaḥ śuciḥ sadityetajjaptantoye 'ghanāśanaṃ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. One will get food by offering an oblation of food with (the recitation of the hymn) annapate\[25\] The repetition of (the hymn) haṃsaḥ śuciṣad (while remaining) in the water destroys sins.

## \|\| 260.38 \|\|

*catvāri bhṛṅgetyetattu sarvvapāpaharaṃ jale \|*  
*devā yajñeti japtvātu brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. (The repetition of the hymn) catvāri śṛṅgāḥ\[27\] (while remaining) in the water will remove all sins. By the repetition of (the hymn) devā yajña one will be respected in the world of Brahmā.

## \|\| 260.39 \|\|

*vasanteti ca hutvājyaṃ ādityādvaramāpnuyāt \|*  
*suparṇosīti cetyasya karmmavyāhṛtivadbhavet \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. One will obtain the favour of the Sun by offering oblation with clarified butter with (the repetition of the hymn) vasanta\[29\]. The rites relating to (the use of the hymn) suparṇo'si\[30\] are the same as for the (seven) vyāhṛtis.

## \|\| 260.40 \|\|

*namaḥ svāheti trirjjaptvā bandhanānmokṣamāpnuyāt \|*  
*antarjjale trirāvartya drupadā sarvvapāpamuk \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. One will get released from bondage by repeating namaḥ svāhā\[32\] three times. By repeating (the hymn) drupadā three times (while remaining) in the water will destroy all sins.

## \|\| 260.41 \|\|

*iha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvaṃ mantroyaṃ buddhivarddhanaḥ \|*  
*hutantu sarpiṣā dadhnā payasā pāyasena vā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The sacred formula iha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvaṃ is capable of sharpening the intellect when oblations are offered with clarified butter, curd, milk and sweet porridge.

## \|\| 260.42 \|\|

*śataṃ ya iti caitena hutvā parṇaphalāṇi ca \|*  
*ārogyaṃ śriyamāpnoti jīvitañca cirantathā \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Oblations made with leaves and fruits with (the recitation of the hymn) śataṃ yo confers health, wealth and long life.

## \|\| 260.43 \|\|

*oṣadhīḥ pratimodagdhvaṃ vapane lavane 'rthakṛt \|*  
*aśvāvatī pāyasena homācchāntimavāpnuyāt \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. (The recitation of the hymn) oṣadhīḥ pratimodadhvaṃ\[36\] while mowing and cutting will give returns. Oblations made with sweet porridge (with the repetition of the hymn) aśvāvat will secure peace.

## \|\| 260.44 \|\|

*tasmā iti ca mantrena bandhanastho vimucyate \|*  
*yuvā suvāsā ityeva vāsāṃsyāpnoti cottamam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. One will be released from bondage by (the repetition of) the sacred formula tasmā\[38\]. One will get excellent dress by (repeating the hymn) yuvā suvāsāḥ.

## \|\| 260.45 \|\|

*muñcantu mā śapathyāni sarvvāntakavināśanam \|*  
*mā māhiṃsīstilājyena hutaṃ ripuvināśanaṃ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. (The recitation of the hymn) muñcantu mā śapathyāt\[40\] is capable of destroying all the enemies. Oblation of sesamum (while reciting the hymn) mā mā hiṃsīḥ is capable of destroying enemies.

## \|\| 260.46 \|\|

*namo 'stu sarvvasarpebhyo ghṛtena pāyasena tu \|*  
*kṛṇudhavaṃ rāja ityetadabhicāravināśanaṃ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. (Oblations of) ghee and sweet porridge (with the repetition of the hymns) namo'stu sarvasarpebhyo\[42\] and kṛṇudhvaṃ rāja destroys magic incantations.

## \|\| 260.47-49 \|\|

*dūrvvākāṇḍāyutaṃ hutvā kāṇḍāt kāṇḍeti mānavaḥ \|*  
*grāme janapade vāpi marakantu śamannayet \|\| 47 \|\|*

*rogārtto mucyate rogāt tathā duḥkhāttu duḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*auḍumbarīśca samidho madhumānno vanaspatiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*hutvā sahasraśo rāma dhanamāpnoti mānavaḥ \|*  
*saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnoti vyavahāre tathā trayam \|\| 49 \|\|*

47-49. One can control an epidemic in a village or country by making ten thousand oblations of pieces of dūrvā grass with (the recitation of the hymn) kāṇḍāt kāṇḍāt\[44\]. One who is suffering from a disease will be cured and the grief-stricken (will become free) from grief (by this). O Rāma! A person who offers a thousand twigs of udumbara (tree)as oblation with (the recitation of the hymn) madhumānno vanaspatiḥ will get wealth. One will also get great fortune and victory in litigation.

## \|\| 260.50-51 \|\|

*apāṃ garbhamiti hutvā devaṃ varṣāpayeddhruvam \|*  
*apaḥ piveti ca tathā hutvā dadhi ghṛtaṃ madhu \|\| 50 \|\|*

*pravarttayati dharmmajña mahāvṛṣṭimanantaraṃ \|*  
*namaste rudra ityetat sarvvopadravanāśanaṃ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. One will make the gods rain by offering oblations (of the same) with (the recitation of the hymn) apāṃ garbhaṃ.\[46\] O Knower of virtue! By making oblations of curd, ghee and honey (with the repetition of the hymn) apaḥ pinva\[47\] one will make it rain heavily. (The repetition of the hymn) namaste rudra destroys all misfortunes.

## \|\| 260.52-53 \|\|

*sarvvaśāntikaraṃ proktaṃ mahāpātakanāśanaṃ \|*  
*adhyavocadityanena rakṣaṇaṃ vyādhitasya tu \|\| 52 \|\|*

*rakṣoghnañca yaśasyañca cirāyuḥpuṣṭivarddhanam \|*  
*siddhārthakānāṃ kṣepeṇa pathi caitajjapan sukhī \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. (The above hymn) is also said to ensure all peace and destroy great sins. One who is afflicted by a disease is protected by (the repetition of the hymn) adhyavocat. It is also capable of destroying demons, increasing fame, long life and strength. One will be happy by scattering white mustard and repeating this (hymn) on the journey.

## \|\| 260.54-56 \|\|

*asau yastāmra ityetat paṭhannityaṃ divākaraṃ \|*  
*upatiṣṭheta dharmajña sāyaṃ prātaratandritaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*annamakṣayamāpnoti dīrghamāyuśca vindati \|*  
*pramuñca dhanvannityetat ṣaḍbhirāyudhamantraṇaṃ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*ripūṇāṃ bhayadaṃ yuddhenātrakāryyā vicāraṇā \|*  
*māno mahānta ityevaṃ bālānāṃ śāntikārakaṃ \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-55a. O Knower of virtue! One will get long life and undiminishing food by worshipping daily the sun morning and evening unweariedly repeating (the hymn) asau yastāmro.

55b-56. Weapons are consecrated by the six (hymns) pramuñca dhanvanas\[51\]. It will frighten enemies in battle. One need not entertain any doubt. (The repetition of the hymn) māno mahāntaṃ confers peace on children.

## \|\| 260.57 \|\|

*namo hiraṇyavāhave ityanuvākasaptakam \|*  
*rājikāṃ kaṭutailāktāṃ juhuyācchatrunāśanīṃ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. One should offer oblations of black mustard soaked in pungent oil (with the repetition of) the seven sections (beginning with) namo hiraṇyabāhave that will destroy enemies.

## \|\| 260.58 \|\|

*namo vaḥ kirikebhyaśca padmalakṣāhutairnnaraḥ \|*  
*rājyalakṣmīmavāpnoti tathā vilvaiḥ suvarṇakam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. One becomes a sovereign by offering oblations of a lakh lotuses with (the recitation of the hymn) namo vaḥ kirikebhyo. By similar (offerings) of bilva (leaves) (one will acquire) gold.

## \|\| 260.59 \|\|

*imā rudrāyeti tilairhomācca dhanamāpyate \|*  
*dūrvāhomena cānyena sarvavyādhivivarjjitaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. One will obtain wealth by oblations of sesamum with (the repetition of) imā rudrāya. Oblations with dūrvā grass (will make one) free from all diseases.

## \|\| 260.60 \|\|

*āśuḥ śiśāna ityetadāyudhānāñca rakṣaṇe \|*  
*saṃgrāme kathitaṃ rāma sarvaśatrunivarhaṇaṃ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. (The hymn) āśuḥ śiśāna (is used) in the protection of weapons. O Rāma! It is said to destroy all the enemies in battle.

## \|\| 260.61 \|\|

*rājasāmeti juhuyāt sahasraṃ pañcabhirdvija \|*  
*ājyāhutīnāṃ dharmajña cakṣūrogādvimucyate \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O Brahmin! Knower of virtue! One thousand oblations of clarified butter with (the repetition of) the five (hymns) rāja sāma will cure the eye disease (of a person).

## \|\| 260.62 \|\|

*śanno vanaspate gehe homaḥ syādvāstudoṣanut \|*  
*agna āyūṃsi hutvājyaṃ dveṣaṃ nāpnoti kenacit \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The oblation (done with the hymn) śanno vanaspate gehe\[58\] will destroy the defects of a building. One will not earn enmity with anyone by offering oblations of clarified butter (with the repetition of) agna āyūṃṣi.

## \|\| 260.63 \|\|

*apāṃ pheneti lājābhirhutvā jayamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*bhadrā itīndriyairhīno japan syāt sakalendriyaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. One will gain victory by the oblation of fried paddy (with the hymn) apāṃ phena\[60\]. He who has defective sense-organs will get sound ones by the repetition of (the hymn) bhadrā.

## \|\| 260.64 \|\|

*agniśca pṛthivī ceti vaśīkaraṇamuttamam \|*  
*adhvaneti japan mantraṃ vyavahāre jayī bhavet \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. (The hymn) agniśca pṛthivī ca\[62\] (is) an excellent charm. One who repeats the hymn adhvana will be victorious in litigation.

## \|\| 260.65 \|\|

*brahma rājanyamiti ca karmārambhe tu siddhikṛt \|*  
*saṃvatsarosīti dhṛtairlakṣahomādarogavān \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. (The hymn) brahma rājanyaṃ\[64\] accomplishes the task (when repeated) at its commencement. One will be free from disease by the oblation of ghee a lakh times (with the repetition of the hymn) saṃvatsaro'si.

## \|\| 260.66 \|\|

*ketuṃ kṛṇvannitītyetat saṃgrāme jayavarddhanam \|*  
*indrognirdharma ityetadraṇe dharmanibandhanam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. (The hymn) ketuṃ kṛṇvan will confer victory in battle.

(The hymn) indro'gnirdharma ensures fair play in battle.

## \|\| 260.67 \|\|

*dhanvā nāgeti mantraśca dhanurgrāhanikaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*yajīteti tathā mantro vijñeyo hyabhimantraṇe \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. The hymn dhanvanā gā\[68\] is excellent for the bow wielder. The hymn yuñjīta is known (to be used) in consecrating (the bow).

## \|\| 260.68 \|\|

*mantraścāhirathetyetaccharāṇāṃ mantraṇe bhavet \|*  
*vahnīnāṃ pitarityetattūṇamantraḥ prakīrttitaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The hymn āhiratha\[70\] should be used for the consecration of arrows. Bahvīnāṃ pitā is said to be the hymn for consecrating quiver.

## \|\| 260.69 \|\|

*yuñjantīti tathāśvānāṃ yojane mantra ucyate \|*  
*āśuḥ śiśāna ityetadyātrārambhaṇamucyate \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Yuñjantī \[Yuñjanti?\]\[72\] is said to be the hymn for arranging horses. (The hymn) āśuḥ śiśāna is said (to be used) while commencing a journey.

## \|\| 260.70 \|\|

*viṣṇoḥ krameti mantraśca rathārohaṇikaḥ paraḥ \|*  
*ājaṅghetīti cāśvānāṃ tāḍanīyamudāhṛtaṃ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The hymns viṣṇoḥ krama\[74\] (is said to be) excellent for one who boards a chariot. (The hymn) ājaṅghanti is said (to be used) for whipping the horses.

## \|\| 260.71 \|\|

*yāḥ senā abhitvarīti parasainyamukhe japet \|*  
*dundubhya iti cāpyetaddundubhītār̤anaṃ bhavet \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. One should repeat (the hymn) yaḥ senā abhitvari\[76\] when facing the army of the enemy. The war drums are beaten with (the recitation of the hymn) dundubhya.

## \|\| 260.72-73 \|\|

*etaiḥ pūrvahutairmantraiḥ kṛtvaivaṃ vijayī bhavet \|*  
*yamena dattamityasya koṭihomādvicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*rathamutpādayecchīghraṃ saṃgrāme vijayapradam \|*  
*ā kṛṣṇeti tathaitasya karmavyāhṛtivadbhavet \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. One will become victorious by offering oblations earlier with these hymns. A wise man who offers one crore oblations with (the recitation of the hymn) yamena dattam\[78\] will soon produce a chariot that will give victory in the battle. The ceremonies relating to (the hymn) ā kṛṣṇa are similar to that of the vyāhṛtis (bhūḥ etc.).

## \|\| 260.74 \|\|

*śivasaṃkalpajāpena samādhiṃ manaso labhet \|*  
*pañcanadyaḥ pañcalakṣaṃ hutvā lakṣmīmavāpnuyāt \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. One will get the composure of mind by the repetition of (the hymn of) śivasaṅkalpa\[80\]. One will get fortune by making five lakh oblations (with the repetition of the hymn) pañcanadyaḥ.

## \|\| 260.75 \|\|

*yadā badhūndākṣāyaṇāṃ mantreṇānena mantritam \|*  
*sahasrakṛtvaḥ kanakaṃ dhārayedripuvāraṇaṃ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. One should wear a golden (plate) after making incantations one thousand times with the hyymn yad ābadhnan dākṣāyaṇā. It will ward off the enemies.

## \|\| 260.76 \|\|

*imaṃ jīvebhya drati ca śilāṃ loṣṭrañcaturddiśaṃ \|*  
*kṣipedgṛhe tadā tasya na syāccaurabhayaṃ niśi \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. One will not have the fear of thieves by throwing stones and lumps of earth in all the four directions in the house (after repeating the hymn) imaṃ jīvebhyaḥ.

## \|\| 260.77 \|\|

*parimegāmaneneti vaśīkaraṇamuttamaṃ \|*  
*hantumabhyāgatastatra vaśībhavati mānavaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. (The hymn) parī me gāmaneṣata is excellent for charming. One who has come to kill will be subdued.

## \|\| 260.78 \|\|

*bhakṣyatāmvūlapuṣpādyaṃ mantritantu prayacchati \|*  
*yasya dharmajña vaśagaḥ somya śīghraṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. O Knower of Dharma! A person will be brought under one’s complete control soon by giving him food, betels, flowers and other things charmed (with this hymn).

## \|\| 260.79-80 \|\|

*śanno mitra itītyetat sadā sarvvatra śāntidaṃ \|*  
*gaṇānāṃ tvā gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā homañcatuṣpathe \|\| 79 \|\|*

*vaśīkuryyājjagatsarvaṃ sarvadhānyairasaṃśayam \|*  
*hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayo mantroyamabhiṣecane \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. (The hymn) śanno mitra\[85\] always confers peace everywhere (when repeated). One will be able to charm the entire world by making oblations of all grains (with the repetition of the hymn) gaṇānāṃ tvā gaṇapatiṃ\[86\] at the junction of four roads. The hymn hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ (is used) in consecration.

## \|\| 260.81-82 \|\|

*śanno devīrabhiṣṭaye tathā śāntikaraḥ paraḥ \|*  
*ekacakreti mantreṇa hutenājyena bhāgaśaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*grahebhyaḥ śāntimāpnoti prasādaṃ na ca saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*gāvo bhaga iti dvābhyāṃ hutvājyaṅgā avāpnuyāt \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. (The hymn) śanno devīr abhiṣṭaye\[88\] (is) excellent for conferring peace. There is no doubt that one will appease the planets and get their grace by offering oblations of clarified butter in parts (to the respective planets) with (the repetition of) the hymn ekacakra\[89\]. One who makes oblations of clarified butter with the two (hymns) gāvo bhago will get cows.

## \|\| 260.83 \|\|

*pravādāṃśaḥ sopaditi gṛhayajñe vidhīyate \|*  
*devebhyo vanaspata iti drumayajñe vidhīyate \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. (The hymn) pravādāṃṣaḥ sopat\[91\] is used in the propitiatory rite in the house. (The hymn) devebhyo vanaspate is prescribed (for use) in the rite for the consecration of a tree.

## \|\| 260.84 \|\|

*gāyatrī vaiṣṇavī jñeyā tadviṣṇoḥ paramampadaṃ \|*  
*sarvvapāpapraśamanaṃ sarvvakāmakarantathā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. (The hymn) tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ is known to be the gāyatrī for (Lord) Viṣṇu. It is capable of destroying all the sins and granting all the pleasures.

## Chapter 261 - The use of the hymns of Sāmaveda (sāmavidhāna)

## \|\| 261.1 \|\|

*puṣkara uvāca \|*  
*yajurvvidhānaṅkathitaṃ vakṣye sāmnāṃ vidhānakaṃ \|*  
*saṃhitāṃ vaiṣṇavīñjaptvā hutvā syāt sarvvakāmabhāk \|\| 1 \|\|*

Puṣkara said:

1\. I have described the use of (the hymns of) Yajur (veda). I shall (now) describe the use of (the hymns of) Sāma (veda) \[i.e., sāmavidhāna\]. One will get all the pleasures by repeating the vaiṣṇavī hymns.

## \|\| 261.2 \|\|

*saṃhitāñchāndasīṃ sādhu japtvā prīṇāti śaṅkaraṃ \|*  
*skāndīṃ paitryāṃ saṃhitāñca japtvā syāttu prasādavān \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. One pleases (Lord) Śaṅkara (Śiva) by repeating the chāndasī (Sāman) hymns well. One will get the grace by repeating the skāndī and paitrī hymns.

## \|\| 261.3 \|\|

*yata indra bhajāmahe hiṃsādoṣavināśanaṃ \|*  
*avakīrṇī mucyate ca agnistigmeti vai japan \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. (The repetition of the hymn) yata indra bhayāmahe\[1\] is capable of destroying the harmful effects (of incantations). One who has broken the vow of continence will be released (from the fault) by repeating (the hymn) agnistigmena.

## \|\| 261.4 \|\|

*sarvvaṃpāpaharaṃ jñeyaṃ paritoyañca tāsu ca \|*  
*avikreyañca vikrīya japedghṛtavatīti ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. (The repetition of the hymn) paritoṣaṃ ca\[3\] is known to be capable of destroying all sins. One who has sold (a thing) that should not be sold, should repeat (the hymn) ghṛtavatī.

## \|\| 261.5-6 \|\|

*ayāno deva savitarjñeyanduḥsvapnanāśanaṃ \|*  
*abodhyagniritimantreṇa ghṛtaṃ rāma yathāvidhi \|\| 5 \|\|*

*abhyukṣya ghṛtaśeṣeṇa mekhalābandha iṣyate \|*  
*strīṇāṃ yāsāntu garbhāṇi patanti bhṛgusattama \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. (The hymn) adyā no deva savitaḥ\[5\] is known to be capable of destroying bad dreams. O Rāma! The foremost of Bhṛgus! It is laid down that the girdle may be tied with the remnant of the ghee that has been sprinkled with (the hymn) abodhyagniḥ as laid down, in the case of the women who have a miscarriage.

## \|\| 261.7 \|\|

*maṇiṃ jātasya bālasya vadhnīyāttadanantaraṃ \|*  
*somaṃ rājānametena vyādhibhirvipramucyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then it should be tied on the wrist of the child that is born, with (the repetition of the hymn) somaṃ rājānaṃ. This will make the child free from all diseases.

## \|\| 261.8-9 \|\|

*sarpasāma prayuñcāno nāpnuyāt sarpajambhayaṃ \|*  
*mādya tvā vādyatetyetaddhutvā vipraḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*satāvarimaṇimbaddhvā nāpnuyācchastrato bhayaṃ \|*  
*dīrghatasasorkka iti hutvānnaṃ prāpnuyādvahu \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. By the use of sarpasāma\[8\] one will not have the fear of serpents. A brahmin will not have any fear from weapons by tying the śatāvarī (a herb) after making a thousand oblations with (the hymn) mādya tvā vādyate\[9\]. One will get plenty of food by making oblation (with the hymn) dīrghatamaso'rka.

## \|\| 261.10 \|\|

*svamadhyāyantīti japanna mriyet pipāsayā \|*  
*tvamimā oṣadhī hyetajjaptvā byādhiṃna vāpnuyāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. One who repeats (the hymn) samamadhyāyantī\[11\] will not die of thirst. One will not get a disease by repeating (the hymn) tvamimā oṣadhīḥ.

## \|\| 261.11 \|\|

*pathi devavratañjaptvā bhayebyo vipramucyate \|*  
*yadindro munaye tveti hutaṃ saubhāgyavarddhanaṃ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. One will become free from fears by repeating (the hymn) devavrata\[13\] on the journey. Oblations offered with (the hymn) yadindro munaye tvā increase fortune.

## \|\| 261.12 \|\|

*bhago na citra hatyevaṃ netrayo rañjanaṃ hitaṃ \|*  
*saubhāgyavarddhanaṃ rāma nātra kāryyā vicāraṇā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O Rāma! Collyrium applied to the eyes (with the hymn) bhago na citra will increase fortune. There need be no doubt.

## \|\| 261.13-14 \|\|

*japedindreti vargañca tathā saubhāgyavarddhanaṃ \|*  
*pari priyā hi vaḥ kāriḥ kābhyāṃ saṃśrāvayet striyaṃ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sā taṅkāmayate rāma nātra kāryyā vicāraṇā \|*  
*rathantaraṃ vāmadevyaṃ brahmavarccasavarddhanaṃ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. The repetition (of the hymn) indreti varga\[16\] will also increase fortune. A man who seeks the love of a woman should make her listen to (the hymn) pari priyā divaḥ kaviḥ\[17\]. O Rāma! There need be no doubt that she will love him in return. (The repetition of the hymns) rathantara\[18\] and vāmadevya increases the divine splendour.

## \|\| 261.15 \|\|

*prāśayedvālakaṃ nityaṃ vacācūrṇaṃ ghṛtaplutaṃ \|*  
*indramidgāthinaṃ japtvā bhavecchrutidharastvasau \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. A child should be fed with the powder of vacā soaked in ghee daily with the repetition of (the hymn) indramidgāthino. It will give him good memory.

## \|\| 261.16 \|\|

*hutvā rathantarañjaptvā putramāpnotyasaṃśayaṃ \|*  
*mayi śrīriti mantroyaṃ japtavyaḥ śrīvivarddhanaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. There is no doubt that one will get progeny after repeating (the hymn) rathantara\[21\] and offering oblations. The hymn mayi śrīḥ has to be repeated for the increase of fortune.

## \|\| 261.17 \|\|

*vairūpyasyāṣṭakaṃ nityaṃ prayuñjānaḥ śriyaṃ labhet \|*  
*saptāṣṭakaṃ prayuñcānaḥ sarvvān kāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The repetition of the eight vairūpya\[23\] (hymns) daily confers fortune. One will get all the desires fulfilled by repeating the saptāṣṭaka (hymns).

## \|\| 261.18 \|\|

*gavyeṣuṇeti yo nityaṃ sāyaṃ prātaratantritaḥ \|*  
*upasthānaṃ gavāṃ kuryyāttasya syustāḥ sadā gṛhe \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. One who worships cows daily morning and evening (with the repetition of the hymn) gavyoṣuṇo unweariedly will always have cows in his house.

## \|\| 261.19 \|\|

*ghṛtāktantu yavadroṇaṃ vāta āvātu bheṣajaṃ \|*  
*anena hutvā vidhivat sarvvāṃ māyāṃ vyapohati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. One who offers a droṇa (a measure) of barley soaked in ghee into fire (with the repetition of the hymn), vāta āvātu bheṣajaṃ as laid down will ward off all spells.

## \|\| 261.20-24 \|\|

*pradevo dāsena tilān hutvā kārmmaṇakṛntanaṃ \|*  
*abhi tvā pūrvvapītaye vaṣaṭa़kārasamanvitaṃ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*vāsakedhmasahasrantu hutaṃ yuddhe jayapradaṃ \|*  
*hastyaśvapuruṣān kuryyād budhaḥ piṣṭamayān śubhān \|\| 21 \|\|*

*parakīyānathoddeśya pradhānapuruṣāṃstathā \|*  
*susvinnān piṣṭakavarān kṣureṇotkṛtya bhāgaśaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*abhi tvā śūra ṇonumo mantreṇānena mantravit \|*  
*kṛtvā sarṣapatailāktān krodhena juhuyāttataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*etat kṛtvā bughaḥ karmma saṃgrāme jayamāpnuyāt \|*  
*gāruḍa़ṃ vāmadevyañca rathantarabṛhadrathau \|\| 24 \|\|*

20-21 a. Oblations of sesamum with (the repetition of the hymn) pra daivo dāso\[27\] destroys witchcraft. (Repeating the hymn) abhi tvā pūrva pītaye \[pitaye?\] followed by the syllable vaṣaṭ while offering oblations made with perfumed fuel will yield victory in battle.

21b-24. A wise man should make good figures of elephants, horses and men with flour and represent the chief men of the enemy with oily cakes of flour and cut them into pieces with a knife. Then the knower of the sacred formulas should offer oblations (with these cakes) soaked in mustard oil with wrath while reciting the hymn abhi tvā śūranonumaḥ.\[29\] The wise man gets victory in battle by this act. The hymns gāruḍa\[30\], vāmadevya,\[31\] rathantara\[32\] and bṛhadratha are without any doubt said to destroy all sins.

## Chapter 262 - The use of the hymns of Atharvaveda (atharvavidhāna)

## \|\| 262.1 \|\|

*puṣkara uvāca \|*  
*sāmnāṃ vidhānaṃ kathitaṃ vakṣaaye cātharvvaṇāmatha \|*  
*śāntātīyaṃ gaṇaṃ hutvā śāntimāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Puṣkara said:

1\. The application of the hymns of Sāma (veda) has been described. I shall describe to you (the application) of (the hymns of) Atharva (veda) \[i.e., atharvavidhāna\]. One gets peace by offering oblations with the hymns of the peace class.

## \|\| 262.2 \|\|

*bhaiṣajyañca gaṇaṃ hutvā sarvvānrogān vyapohati \|*  
*trisaptīyaṃ gaṇaṃ hutvā sarvvapapaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. One will get rid of all the diseases by offering oblations to (the gods of) the remedial class. One will get free from all sins by offering oblations to (the gods of) the trisaptīya class.

## \|\| 262.3 \|\|

*kkacinnāpnoti ca bhayaṃ hutvā caivābhayaṅgaṇaṃ \|*  
*na kkacijjāyate rāma gaṇaṃ hutvā parājitaṃ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. One will never get fear by offering oblations to (the gods of) the protection class. O Rāma! one will never be born by offering oblations to (the gods of) the aparājita (unconquered) class.

## \|\| 262.4 \|\|

*āyuṣyañca gaṇaṃ hutvā apamṛtyuṃ vyapohati \|*  
*svastimāpnoti sarvvatra hutvā svastyanaṅgaṇaṃ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. One will ward off untimely death by offering oblations to (the gods of) the life-giving class. One will get welfare everywhere by offering oblations to (the gods of) the welfare class.

## \|\| 262.5 \|\|

*śreyasā yogamāpnoti śarmmavarmmagaṇantathā \|*  
*vāstoṣpatyagaṇaṃ hutvā vāstudoṣān vyapohati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. One will get united with good fortune (by propitiating the gods of) happiness and armour group. One will remove the defects of a building by offering oblations to the class of deities presiding over the foundations of a house.

## \|\| 262.6 \|\|

*tathā raudragaṇaṃ hutvā sarvvān doṣān vyaṣohati \|*  
*etairdaśaguṇairhomo hyaṣṭādaśasu śāntiṣu \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. In the same way one will remove all the defects by offering oblations to (the gods of) the Raudra class. Oblations (are to be offered to) these ten classes in eighteen propitiatory (rites).

## \|\| 262.7-9 \|\|

*vaiṣṇavī śāntiraindrī ca vrāhmī raudrī tathaiva ca \|*  
*vāyavyā vāruṇī caiva kauverī bhārgavī tathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*prājāpatyā tathā tvāṣṭrī kaumārī vahnidevatā \|*  
*mārudgaṇā ca gāndhārī śāntirnairṛtakī tathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śāntirāṅgirasī yāmyā pārthivī sarvvakāmadā \|*  
*yastvāṃ mṛtyuriti hyetajjaptaṃ mṛtyuvināśanaṃ \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. (The goddesses) Vaiṣṇavī, Śānti, Aindrī, Brāhmī, Raudrī, Vāyavyā, Vāruṇī, Kauberī, Bhārgavī, Prājāpatyā, Tvāṣṭrī, Kaumārī, Vahnidevatā, Mārudgaṇā, Gāndhārī, Śānti Nairṛtakī, Śānti Āṅgirasī, Yāmyā and Pārthivī (are the eighteen propitiatory items) that yield all pleasures. The recitation (of the hymn) yastvā mṛtyuḥ conquers death.

## \|\| 262.10 \|\|

*suparṇaṃstveti hutvā ca bhujagairnaiva bādhyate \|*  
*indreṇa dattamityetat sarvakāmakarambhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. One will never be afflicted by serpents by offering oblations with (the hymn) suparṇastvā\[2\]! (The hymn) indreṇa dattaṃ confers all the pleasures.

## \|\| 262.11 \|\|

*indreṇa dattamityetat sarvabādhāvināśanaṃ \|*  
*imā devīti mantraśca sarvaśāntikaraḥ paraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. (The hymn) indreṇa dattam\[4\] is capable of destroying all obstacles. The hymn imā devī is an excellent all-appeasing (hymn).

## \|\| 262.12 \|\|

*devā maruta ityetat sarvakāmakarambhavet \|*  
*yamasya lokādityett duḥsvapnaśamanamparaṃ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. (The hymn) devā maruta\[6\] confers all the pleasures. (The hymn) yamasya lokāt is excellent for removing (the effects of) bad dreams.

## \|\| 262.13 \|\|

*indraśca pañcabaṇijeti1 paṇyalābhakaraṃ paraṃ \|*  
*kāmo me vājīti hutaṃ strīṇāṃ saubāgyavarddhanaṃ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. (The hymn) indraśca pañcavaṇijā\[8\] is excellent for profit in trade. Oblations offered with (the hymn) kāmo me vāji increase the fortune of women.

## \|\| 262.14 \|\|

*tubhyameva jabīmannityayutantu hutambhavet \|*  
*agnegobinna ityetat2 medhāvṛddhikaramparaṃ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Oblation offered a lakh times with (the repetition of the hymn) tubhyameva jariman\[10\] and with (the hymn) agne gobhir na will promote the intellect.

## \|\| 262.15 \|\|

*dhruvaṃ dhruveṇeti hutaṃ sthānalābhakaraṃ bhavet \|*  
*alaktajīveti śunā kṛṣilābhakaraṃ bhavet \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Offering oblation with (the hymn) dhruvaṃ dhruveṇa\[12\] will ensure the acquisition of land. The repetition of (the hymn) alaktakajīva will ensure prosperous agriculture.

## \|\| 262.16 \|\|

*ahante bhagna ityetat bhavetsaubhāgyavarddhanaṃ \|*  
*ye me pāśāstathāpyetat bandhanānmokṣakāraṇaṃ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. (The hymn) ahaṃ te bhagna\[14\] increases fortune. (The hymn) ye mepāśāḥ secures release from bondage.

## \|\| 262.17 \|\|

*śapatvahanniti ripūn nāśayeddhomajāpyataḥ \|*  
*tvamuttamamitītyetadyaśobuddhivivarddhanaṃ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Oblation offered with the repetition of (the hymn) śapatvahan\[16\] destroys enemies. (The hymn) tvamuttamam is capable of increasing fame and intellect.

## \|\| 262.18 \|\|

*yathā mṛgamatītyetat strīṇāṃ saubhāgyavarddhanaṃ \|*  
*yena cehadidañcaiva garbhalābhakaraṃ bhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. (The hymn) yathā mṛgamatī\[18\] increases the good fortune of women. (The hymn) yena cehadiśaṃ is advantageous for conception.

## \|\| 262.19 \|\|

*atyante yonirityetat putralābhakaraṃ bhavet \|*  
*śivaḥ śivābhirityetat bhavetsaubhāgyavarddhanaṃ3 \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. (The hymn) ayaṃ te yoniḥ\[20\] is favourable for progeny. (The hymn) śivaḥ śivābhiḥ increases good fortune.

## \|\| 262.20 \|\|

*vṛhaspatirnnaḥ paripātu pathi svastyayanaṃ bhavet \|*  
*muñaacāmi tveti kathitamapamṛtyunivāraṇaṃ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. (The repetition of the hymn) bṛhaspatirnaḥ paripātu\[22\] secures safety on the journey. (The hymn) muñcāmi tvā is said to ward off untimely death.

## \|\| 262.21 \|\|

*atharvaśiraso'dyetā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*prādhānyena tu mantrāṇāṃ kiñcit karma taveritaṃ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. One who masters the atharvaśiras becomes free from all sins. I have described to you some procedures relating to some important hymns.

## \|\| 262.22-25 \|\|

*vṛkṣāṇaāṃ yajñiyānāntu samidhaḥ prathamaṃ haviḥ \|*  
*ājyañca vrīhayaścaiva tathā vai gaurasarṣapāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*akṣatāni tilāścaiva dadhikṣīre ca bhārgava \|*  
*darbhāstathaiva dūrvāśca vilvāni kamalāni ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śāntipuṣṭikarāṇyāhurdravyāṇyetāni sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*tailaṅkaṇāni dharmajña rājikā rudhiraṃ viṣaṃ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*samidhaḥ kaṇṭakopetā abhicāreṣu yojayet \|*  
*ārṣaṃ vai daivataṃ chando binyogajña ācaret \|\| 25 \|\|*

22-24a. The first material for oblations is the twigs of trees suitable for such rites. O Bhārgava! Clarified butter, rice, white mustard, unbroken rice, sesamum, curd, milk, darbha (grass), dūrvā (grass), bilva (leaves) and lotuses are always said to be the materials that promote peace and prosperity.

24b-25. O Knower of righteousness! Mustard oil, blood, poison, twigs of thorny (trees) should be used in magic incantations. One who knows the employment should repeat the sage, deity and metre (relating to the hymns).

## Chapter 263 - Appeasing rites for portents (utpāta-śānti)

## \|\| 263.1 \|\|

*puṣkara uvāca \|*  
*śrīsūktaṃ prativedañca kṣeyaṃ lakṣaamīvivarddhanaṃ \|*  
*hiraṇyavarṇā hariṇīmṛcaḥ pañcadaśa śriyaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Puṣkara said:

1\. The śrīsūkta of each Veda is known to be capable of increasing fortune. The fifteen hymns (beginning with) hiraṇyavarṇāṃ hariṇīṃ (are considered to be conferring) fortune.

## \|\| 263.2 \|\|

*ratheṣvakṣeṣu vājeti catasro yajuṣi śriyaḥ \|*  
*srāvantīyaṃ tathā sāma śrīsūktaṃ sāmavedake \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The four hymns ratheṣvakṣeṣu vṛṣabha\[2\] in the Yajur (Veda) (are said to confer) fortune. The Sāma hymns srāvantīyaṃ is the śrīsūkta in the Sāmaveda.

## \|\| 263.3 \|\|

*śriyaṃ dhātarmayi dhehi proktamātharvaṇe tathā \|*  
*śrīsūktaṃ yo japedbhaktyā hatvā śrīstasya vai bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the same way, (the hymn) śriyaṃ dhātamayi dhehi in the Atharvaveda is said (to be conferring fortune). One who repeats the śrīsūkta with devotion and offers oblation gets fortune.

## \|\| 263.4 \|\|

*padmāni cātha vilvāni hutvājyaṃ vā lilān śriyaḥ \|*  
*ekantu pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ prativedantu sarvadaṃ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. One will get fortune by offering oblations of lotuses, bilva (leaves), clarified butter and sesamum. The puruṣasūkta is the same for each one of the Vedas. It gives everything.

## \|\| 263.5 \|\|

*sūktena dadyānniṣpāpo hyekaikayā1 jalāñjaliṃ \|*  
*snāta ekaikayā puṣpaṃ viṣṇorddatvāghahā bhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. If libation of water is presented with (the recitation of) each one of the hymns, it will make one free from sin. One will destroy his sins by offering flowers to Viṣṇu with each one (of the hymns) after bathing.

## \|\| 263.6 \|\|

*snāta ekaikayā datvā phalaṃ syāt sarvakāmabhāk \|*  
*mahāpāpopapāpānto bhavejjaptvā tu pairuṣaṃ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. One would get all the pleasures by giving away a fruit with each one (of the hymns) after bathing. By the repetition of the Puruṣasūkta major and minor sins are destroyed.

## \|\| 263.7 \|\|

*kṛcchrairviśuddho japtvā ca hutvā snātvā'tha sarvabhāk \|*  
*aṣṭādaśabhyaḥ sāntibhyastisro'nyāḥ śāntayo varāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. One gets everything by repeating the kṛcchra (hymns) and offering oblations (with them) after becoming clean by bathing. Three other appeasing (hymns) besides the eighteen appeasing (hymns) are excellent.

## \|\| 263.8-10 \|\|

*amṛtā cābhyā saumyā sarvvotpātavimarddanāḥ \|*  
*amṛtā sarvadaivatyā abhyā brahmadaivatā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*saumyā ca sarvadaivatyā ekā syātsarvvakāmadā \|*  
*abhayāyāmaṇiḥ kāryyo varuṇasya bhṛgūttama \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śatakāṇḍo'mṛtāyāśca saumyāyāḥ śaṅkhajo maṇiḥ \|*  
*taddaivatyāstathā mantrāḥ siddhau syānmaṇibandhanaṃ \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Amṛtā, abhayā and saumyā destory all the calamities. Amṛtā (is governed) by all the gods. Abhayā (is governed) by Brahmā and Saumyā by all gods. Any one (of them will) confer all the pleasures. O Foremost among Bhṛgus! The wristlet with the Varuṇa (hymn) is to be prepared for the abhayā appeasement. Similarly śatakāṇḍa is (for the wristlet) for amṛtā and conch for saumyā. In order to accomplish (the desired results) the respective hymns of the deities should be used for the wristlets.

## \|\| 263.11-13 \|\|

*divyāntarīkṣabhaumādisamutpātārdanāimāḥ \|*  
*dvivyāntarīkṣabhaumantu adbhutaṃ trividhaṃ śrṛṇu \|\| 11 \|\|*

*graharkṣavaikṛtaṃ divyamāntarīkṣannibodha me \|*  
*ulkāpātaśca digdāhaḥ pariveśastathaiva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*gandharvanagarañcaiva vṛṣṭiśca vikṛtā ca yā \|*  
*carasthirabhavaṃ bhūmau bhūkampamapi bhūmijaṃ \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. These are capable of destroying the calamities relating to the heavens, atmosphere and earth. Listen to me! (I shall describe) the supernatural events relating to the heavens, atmosphere and the earth. You learn from me that (the phenomena) relating to the heavens are caused by the ruling asterisms of the day. (Those) of the sky are the fall of a meteor, scorching glow in the directions, the halo around the sun or moon, (the appearance of) fairy towns and rains. (The phenomena) relating to the earth are the extraordinary events affecting the movable and immovable things and earthquake.

## \|\| 263.14 \|\|

*saptāhābhyantare vaṣṭāvadbhutaṃ niṣphalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*śāntiṃ vinā tribhirvarṣairadbhutaṃ bhayakṛdbhavet \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The portent will not bear any fruit if it rains within seven days. A portent without any appeasement within three years is very dangerous.

## \|\| 263.15-17 \|\|

*devatārccāḥ pranṛtyanti vepante prajvalanti ca \|*  
*āraṭhanti ca rodanti prasvidyantehasanti ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*arccāvikāropaśamo'bhyarcya hutvā prajāpateḥ \|*  
*anagnirdīpyate yatra rāṣṭre ca bhṛśanisvanaṃ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*na dīpyate cendhanavāṃstadrāṣṭraṃ pīḍyate nṛpaiḥ \|*  
*agnivaikṛtyaśamanamagnimantraiśca bhārgava \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-16a. The images of gods will dance, shake, glow, shout, weep, perspire and laugh. (These are portents.) The changes in the images can be pacified by worshipping (Lord) Prajāpati (Brahmā) and offering oblations.

16b-17. When there is blaze in a country without fire, with loud noise and without fuel that burns, that country will be tormented by kings. O Son of Bhṛgu! The change in the fire is appeased with the hymns of Fire (god).

## \|\| 263.18 \|\|

*akāle phalitā vṛkṣāḥ kṣīraṃ raktaṃ sravanti ca \|*  
*vṛkṣotpātapraśamanaṃ śivaṃ pūjya ca kārayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. When the trees bear fruit out of season, ooze out milk and blood, one should do the appeasing rite for the portents after worshipping (Lord) Śiva.

## \|\| 263.19-21 \|\|

*ativṛṣṭiranāvṛṣṭirdurbhikṣāyobhayaṃ mataṃ \|*  
*anṛtau tridinārabghavṛṣṭirjñeyā bhayāya hi \|\| 19 \|\|*

*vṛṣṭivaikṛtyanāśaḥ syātparjanyendvarkapūjanāt \|*  
*nagarādapasarpante samīpamupayānti ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

*nadyo hradapraśravaṇā virasāśca bhavanti ca \|*  
*salilāśayavaikṛtye japtavyo vāruṇo manuḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-20a. Both excessive rains and draught are considered to give rise to famine. Rain occurring consecutively for three days out of season is known (to be a portent) of danger. The change in (the pattern of) rain is nullified by the worship of Parjanya (Rain god), Moon and Sun.

20b-21. If rivers recede from the cities or come near them, if they flow gushing forth or get dried up, then the Varuṇa hymn should be recited as also in the case of deterioration in the (state of) the reservoirs.

## \|\| 263.22-31 \|\|

*akālaprasavā nāryyaḥ kālato vāprajāstathā \|*  
*vikṛtaprasavāścaiva yugmaprasavanādikaṃ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*strīṇāṃ prasavavaikṛtye strīviprādi prapūjayet \|*  
*vaḍa़vā hastinī gaurvā yadi yugmaṃ prasūyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vijātyaṃ vikṛtaṃ vāpi ṣaḍbhirmāsairmriyet vai \|*  
*vikṛtaṃ vā prasūyante paracakrabhayaṃ bhavet \|\| 24 \|\|*

*homaḥ prasūtivaikṛtye japo viprādipūjanaṃ \|*  
*yāni yānānyayuktāni yuktāni na vahanti ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ākāśe tūryanādāśca mahadbhayamupasthitaṃ \|*  
*praviśanti yadā grāmamāraṇyā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*araṇyaṃ yānti vā grāmyāḥ jalaṃ yānti sthalodbhavāḥ \|*  
*sthalaṃ vā jalajā yānti rājādvārādike śivāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*pradoṣe kukkuṭo vāse śivā cārkodaye bhavet \|*  
*gṛhaṅkapotaḥ praviśet kravyādvā mūrdidhna līyate \|\| 28 \|\|*

*madhurāṃ makṣikāṃ kuryyāṃt kāko maithunago dṛśi \|*  
*prāsādatoraṇodyānadvāraprākāraveśmanāṃ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*animittantu patanaṃ dṛḍha़ाnāṃ rājamṛtyave \|*  
*rajasā vātha kadhūmena diśo yatra samākulāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*ketūdayoparāgau ca chidratā śaśisūryayoḥ \|*  
*graharkṣavikṛtiryatra tatrāpi bhayamādiśet \|\| 31 \|\|*

22-23a. The women may deliver prematurely or may not deliver at the appropriate time. They may deliver children with deformities or deliver twins etc. One should worship the women and brahmins in the case of such deviations in the delivery (as above).

23b-25a. If a mare or she-elephant or cow gives birth to twins or to deformed younger or to ones different from the species, it will die within six months. In the case of deformed youngs there will be danger from hostile forces. The recitation and oblation as well as worship of brahmins should be done (in such cases).

25b-26a. If vehicles run without being yoked (to steeds), if (vehicles) yoked (to steeds) do not run, or trumpet sounds (are heard) in the sky, then it forebodes great impending danger.

26b-30a. If wild animals and birds enter village and those of village enter forest; land (animals) enter water and water (animals) enter land, vixens howl at the threshold of a palace, cocks crow at pradoṣa (the time preceding the night fall); vixens howl at the residence or at the rising Sun; dove enters the house, carnivorous birds stoop down on the head; bees make sweet (sound); crows mate in sight; strong arches of palace, garden, door-ways, corridor and mansions fall without an obvious cause, it forebodes evil. (It forebodes) the death of the king.

30b-31. If the quarters are filled by dust or smoke, if (the country is) under the influence of the descending node, if spots in the moon and sun are visible, or if the stars and planets are not to be seen, it also indicates fear.

## \|\| 263.32 \|\|

*agniryatra na dīpyeta stravante codakumbhakāḥ \|*  
*mṛtirbhayaṃ śūnytādirutpātānāṃ phalambhavet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Where the fire does not glow, the waterpots ooze, there is the fear of death and witchcraft as the result of the portents. The portent is appeased by the worship of brahmins and gods, recitation of hymns and offer of oblations.

## Chapter 264 - Worship of gods to ward off the effects of portents (devapūjā)

## \|\| 264.1 \|\|

*atha triṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ \|*  
*devapūjāvaiśvadevabaliḥ \|*  
*puṣkara uvāca \|*  
*devapūjādikaṃ karma vakṣye cotpātamardanam \|*  
*āpohiṣṭeti tisṛbhiḥ snāto 'rghyaṃ viṣṇaverpayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

\[Full title: Worship of gods to ward off the effects of portents (devapūjā) and mode of offering the Vaiśvadeva ball (vaiśvadevabali)\]

Puṣkara said:

1\. I shall describe the mode of worshipping the gods and other rites that destroy (the effects of) portents. One should offer respectful water of libation to (Lord) Viṣṇu with the three (hymns beginning with) āpo hi ṣṭhā after having bathed.

## \|\| 264.2 \|\|

*hiraṇyavarṇā iti ca pādyañca tisṛbhirdvija \|*  
*śanna āpo hyācamanamidamāpo 'bhiṣecanaṃ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. O Brahmin! Water for washing the feet (should be offered) with the three (hymns beginning with) hiraṇyavarṇa\[2\]. Water for sipping (is offered with the recitation of the hymn) śanna āpo\[3\] and for bathing with (the hymn) idamāpaḥ.

## \|\| 264.3 \|\|

*rathe akṣe ca tisṛbhirgandhaṃ yuveti vastrakaṃ \|*  
*puṣpaṃ puṣpavatītyevaṃ dhūpandhūposi cāpyatha \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Perfumes (are offered) with the three (hymns) rathe akṣe\[5\] and dress with (the hymn) yuva\[6\]. Flowers (are given) with (the recitation of the hymn) puṣpavatīḥ\[7\] and incense with (the hymn) dhūpo'si.

## \|\| 264.4-6 \|\|

*tejosi śukraṃ dīpaṃ syānmadhuparkaṃ dadhīti ca \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbha ityaṣṭāvṛcaḥ proktā nivedane \|\| 4 \|\|*

*annasya manujaśreṣṭha pānasya ca sugandhinaḥ \|*  
*cāmaravyajanopānacchatraṃ yānāsane tathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*yat kiñcidevamādi syātsāvitreṇa nivedayet \|*  
*pauruṣantu japet sūktaṃ tadeva juhuyāttathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. (The hymn for offering) the lamp is tejo’si\[9\] and for the madhuparka\[10\], dadhi\[11\]. O Foremost among men! The eight hymns (beginning) with hiraṇyagarbhaḥ\[12\] are said to be (used) in offering eatables (to gods), cooked rice, drinks, perfume, chowrie, fan, shoe, umbrella, chariot and seat. Whatever other thing has to be offered should be accompanied by the recitation of (the hymn) of (god) Savitṛ. The puruṣasūkta should be repeated and oblations should be offered with the same (hymn).

## \|\| 264.7 \|\|

*arccābhāve tathā vedyāñjale pūrṇaghaṭe tathā \|*  
*nadītīre 'tha kamale śāntiḥ syādviṣṇupūjanāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In the absence of an image (of Lord Viṣṇu) (the deity should be invoked) on the altar or in water or in a pot full (with water) or on the banks of a river or in a lotus. One would thus accomplish the propitiation by worshipping (lord) Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 264.8-12 \|\|

*tato homaḥ prakarttavyo dīpyamāne vibhāvasau \|*  
*parisammṛjya paryyukṣya paristīryya paristaraiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sarvvānnāgraṃ samuddhṛtya juhuyāt prayatastataḥ \|*  
*vāsudevāya devāya prabhave cāvyayāya ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*agnaye caiva somāya mitrāya varuṇāya ca \|*  
*indrāya ca mahābhāga indrāgnibhyāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

*viśvebhyaścaiva devebhyaḥ prajānāṃ pataye namaḥ \|*  
*anumatyai tathā rāma dhanvantaraya eva ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vāstoṣpatyai tato devyai tataḥ sviṣṭikṛte 'gnaye \|*  
*sacaturthyantanāmnā tu hutvaitebhyo baliṃ haret \|\| 12 \|\|*

8-12. Then the oblations should be offered to the glowing fire with the entire food being collected and offered with earnestness after cleaning the ground, sprinkling water and spreading sand and kuśa grass. (One should say) (obeisance) to Vāsudeva, to the lord, to the master, to the immutable, to the Fire (god), to Soma\[14\], to Mitra, to Varuṇa and to Indra. O Fortunate one Obeisance to Indra and Fire (god), the Viśvedevas\[15\] and to the lord of the beings. Oh! Rāma! Then (one should say) (obeisance) to Anumati\[16\], to Dhanvantari\[17\], to Vāstoṣpati, to the goddess, to the Fire that accomplishes the sacrificial rite. After having made the oblations (thus) with the names ending in the dative case, a part of the offering is given away as gift.

## \|\| 264.13-14 \|\|

*takṣopatakṣamabhitaḥ pūrveṇāgnimataḥ param \|*  
*aśvānāmapi dharmajña ūrṇānāmāni cāpyatha \|\| 13 \|\|*

*nirundhī dhūmriṇīkā ca asvapantī tathaiva ca \|*  
*meghapatnī ca nāmāni sarvveṣāmeva bhārgava \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. O Son of Bhṛgu! Knower of righteousness! Takṣa and Upatakṣa towards the east, then the horses and the hairs (on the south), Nirundhī and Dhūmriṇīkā (on the west) and Asvapantī and Meghapatnī (on the north) are the names of all those (to be worshipped) all around (in a circle).

## \|\| 264.15-16 \|\|

*āgneyādyāḥ krameṇātha tataḥ śaktiṣu nikṣipet \|*  
*nandinyai ca subhāgyai ca sumaṅgalyai ca bhārgava \|\| 15 \|\|*

*1 sacaturthīkanāmneti pāṭhaḥ sādhuḥ \|*  
*bhadrakālyai tato datvā sthūṇāyāñca tathā śriye \|*  
*hiraṇyakeśyai ca tathā vanaspataya eva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. The Fire-god and other gods should be located in (the places of) the goddesses. O Son of Bhṛgu! (goddesses) Nandinī, Subhāgyā, Sumaṅgalī, Bhadrakālī, Sthūṇā, Śrī, Hiraṇyakeśī and Vanaspati are worshipped.

## \|\| 264.17-22 \|\|

*dharmmādharmamayau dvāre gṛhamadhye dhruvāya ca \|*  
*mṛtyave ca vahirdadyādvaruṇāyodakāśaye \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bhūtebhyaśca bahirddadyāccharaṇe dhanadāya ca \|*  
*indrāyendrapuruṣebhyo dadyāt pūrveṇa mānavaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*yamāya tatpuruṣebhyo dadyāddakṣiṇatastathā \|*  
*varuṇāya tatpuruṣebhyo dadyātpaścimatastathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*somāya somapuruṣebhya udagdadyādanantaraṃ \|*  
*brahmaṇe brahmapuruṣebhyo madhye dadyāttathaiva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ākāśe ca tathā corddhve sthaṇḍilāya kṣitau tathā \|*  
*divā divācarebhyaśca rātrau rātricareṣu ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

*baliṃ vahistathā dadyātsāyaṃ prātastu pratyahaṃ \|*  
*piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ kuryyāt prātaḥ sāyanna kārayet \|\| 22 \|\|*

17-22. Offering is made to Dharma and Adharma at the door, Dhruva at the centre of the house, Mṛtyu outside, Varuṇa at a reservoir, the goblins outside (the house), the god of wealth at the house, Indra and companions on the east, Yama and his attendants on the south, Varuṇa and his companions on the west and Soma and his attendants on the north. (Offering) is made to Brahmā and his attendants at the centre. (Offerings) should be made in the sky, above, on the floor and on the earth during the day (for the spirits) that wander during the day and in the night for those that wander during the night. Offering should be made (to the spirits) morning and evening daily outside. Then offering of balls of rice is made (for the manes). It should not be done in the evening.

## \|\| 264.23-28 \|\|

*pitre tu prathamaṃ dadyāttatpitre tadanantaram \|*  
*prapitāmahāya tanmātre pitṛmātre tato 'rpayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tanmātre dakṣiṇāgreṣu kuśeṣvevaṃ yajet pitṝn \|*  
*indravāruṇavāyavyā yāmyā vā nairṛtāśca ye \|\| 24 \|\|*

*te kākāḥ pratigṛhṇantu imaṃ piṇḍaṃ mayodvṛtam \|*  
*kākapiṇḍantu mantreṇa śunaḥ piṇḍaṃ pradāpayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vivasvataḥ kule jātau dvau śyāvaśabalau śunau \|*  
*teṣāṃ piṇḍaṃ pradāsyāmi pathi rakṣantu me sadā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*saurabheyyaḥ sarvahitāḥ pavitrāḥ pāpanāśanāḥ \|*  
*pratigṛhṇantu me grāsaṃ gāvastrailokyamātaraḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*grogrāsañca svastyayanaṃ kṛtvā bhikṣāṃ pradāpayet \|*  
*atithīndīnān pūjayitvā gṛhī bhuñjīta ca svayaṃ \|\| 28 \|\|*

23-28. Offering is first made to (the dead) father, then to the grandfather and great-gradfather, then to one’s mother, paternal grandmother and paternal great-grandmother. The manes should thus be worshipped on the kuśa (grass) having their tips facing the south. The offerings of balls of rice to the crows are made with the repetition of the sacred formula stating ‘let the crows partake in the directions of east, west, north-west, south and south-west’. (Similarly) the ball of rice to the dogs is offered (with the repetition of the sacred formula, ‘I am offering the ball of rice to the dogs in the family of Sun that are black and of variegated colours. May it protect me always on the path to the next world’).
